data.description:
Prerequisite epic for the test creation calibration program (d566-afa6, 7f42-e41f, 69e8-af39, 411b-a047). Depends on the Closure Checks schema migration epic.

## Problem

When parallel sub-agents in /dso:sprint each reference the same parent epic's SCs without coordination, they unknowingly write duplicate behavioral tests for the same intent items. Today there is no structural mechanism preventing this — dedup is a runtime hope, not a guarantee.

## Goal

During /dso:preplanning and /dso:implementation-plan, partition every end-state intent item (SC at epic level, DoD at story level, AC at task level) into a structured intent-allocation manifest that assigns:
- **owner_ticket**: exactly one descendant ticket that will write and maintain the durable test for this intent item.
- **test_artifact**: the test file path (and ideally test name) where the durable test will live.

Contribution is shared and inherited from the parent-child ticket structure — multiple tickets may implement code that satisfies the SC, but exactly one owns the durable test.

## Test ownership model (worked example)

> Epic SC: 'Users can export results as CSV'
> - Story A (backend): Tasks A.1 (SQL builder), A.2 (CSV serializer), A.3 (HTTP streaming)
> - Story B (frontend): Tasks B.1 (button + click handler), B.2 (download + error toast)
>
> Allocation:
> - epic-SC-1 → owner: A.3, test_artifact: tests/integration/test_csv_export.py::test_user_downloads_csv
> - story-A-DoD-1 'POST /export returns valid CSV' → owner: A.3
> - task-A.2-AC-1 'serializer handles empty dict' → owner: A.2
> - task-B.2-AC-1 'error toast on 500' → owner: B.2
> (Contributors A.1, A.2, B.1, B.2 implement code the epic SC test exercises, but do not write a duplicate epic-SC-level test.)

## Components

- Contract: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-allocation-manifest.md (schema, validation rules, dedup detection).
- Brainstorm output: epic-level SC list includes proposed scenario decomposition (when one SC needs multiple tests).
- Preplanning output: per-story DoD list + proposed owner_ticket allocation for each parent SC scenario.
- Implementation-plan output: per-task AC list + proposed owner_ticket allocation for each parent DoD; final allocation manifest published to the ticket tree.
- Pre-commit check: every end-state intent item has exactly one owner_ticket; flag orphans (no owner) and conflicts (multiple owners).
- Test-writer consumption: each task arrives with claimable_intent: [list of intent items this task owns + must produce test artifacts for].

## Dedup detection (the original duplication concern)

Strict: two tickets registering owner-level tests for the same intent item is a hard error. Soft: same parent intent decomposed into legitimately distinct scenarios is allowed and is the recommended path when one SC needs multiple tests (each scenario is a separate intent item with its own owner).

## Out of scope

- Closure Checks schema cleavage (prerequisite, separate epic).
- Test-writing prompt rules consuming the manifest (d566-afa6, depends on this).
- Mutation-kill verification against the manifest (411b-a047, depends on this).
- Suite growth metrics (7f42-e41f, depends on this).

## Dependents

d566-afa6 (test-writer prompt rules consume the manifest), 7f42-e41f (growth metrics computed per intent item), 411b-a047 (mutation verification keyed by intent item), 69e8-af39 (feedback loop tags missed bugs against intent items).

Refine via /dso:brainstorm.
data.title: Plan-time intent allocation: assign owner_ticket + test_artifact to every end-state intent item before implementation begins
